en: Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Bishr—meaning Ibn al-Mufaddal—narrated to us [H]; and 'Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di narrated to us: Isma'il—meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us; both of them from Sa'id ibn Yazid, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Among your caliphs there will be a caliph who will scoop up wealth in handfuls, not counting it at all.' And in the narration of Ibn Hujr: 'scoops up wealth.'
And Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Sa'id—meaning al-Jurayri—narrated to us, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's—both saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, who said: We were with Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, and he said: 'It is near that neither a qafiz nor a dirham will be brought to the people of Iraq.' We said: 'From where will that be?' He said: 'From the direction of the non-Arabs, who will prevent that.' Then he said: 'It is near that neither a dinar nor a mudy will be brought to the people of ash-Sham.' We said: 'From where will that be?' He said: 'From the direction of the Byzantines.' Then he remained silent for a short while, and then said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'At the end of my Ummah there will be a caliph who will scoop up wealth in handfuls, not counting it at all.' He said: I said to Abu Nadrah and Abu al-'Ala': 'Do you two think that it is 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz?' They said: 'No.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id and Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'At the end of time there will be a caliph who distributes wealth and does not count it.'

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki' and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Shortly before the Hour you will fight a people whose shoes are of hair, whose faces are like hammered shields, red-faced with small eyes.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until the Muslims fight the Turks, a people whose faces are like hammered shields, who wear clothes of hair and walk in shoes of hair.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, tracing it back to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'The Hour will not be established until you fight a people whose shoes are of hair, and the Hour will not be established until you fight a people with small eyes and flat, upturned noses.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until a nation fights you whose shoes are of hair, and whose faces are like hammered shields.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi 'Umar's—both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until you fight a people whose faces are like hammered shields, and the Hour will not be established until you fight a people whose shoes are of hair.'

Muhammad ibn Bashshar al-'Abdi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Kabir ibn 'Abd al-Majid Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Hakam narrating from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'Days and nights will not pass away until a man called al-Jahjah rules.' Muslim said: They are four brothers: Sharik, 'Ubaydullah, 'Umayr, and 'Abd al-Kabir, sons of 'Abd al-Majid.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—informed us, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until a man from Qahtan emerges driving the people with his staff.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning ad-Darawardi—narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Dhu as-Suwayqatayn from Abyssinia will destroy the House of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Dhu as-Suwayqatayn from Abyssinia will destroy the Ka'bah.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's—both saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Sa'd, from az-Zuhri, from Sa'id, who heard Abu Hurayrah saying from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): 'Dhu as-Suwayqatayn from Abyssinia will destroy the Ka'bah.'

'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Aban and Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abu Isma'il al-Aslami, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the world will not pass away until there comes upon the people a day in which the killer does not know why he killed, nor the killed why he was killed.' It was said: 'How will that be?' He said: 'Turmoil. The killer and the killed are in the Fire.' And in the narration of Ibn Aban he said: 'he is Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Isma'il,' and he did not mention al-Aslami.

Ibn Abi 'Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Marwan narrated to us, from Yazid—and he is Ibn Kaysan—from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there will surely come upon the people a time when the killer will not know for what he killed, nor will the killed know for what he was killed.'
And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Abu Bakr—and he is al-Hanafi—narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari and Abu Ma'n Zayd ibn Yazid ar-Raqashi narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Ma'n's—both saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn al-'Ala', from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'Night and day will not pass away until al-Lat and al-'Uzza are worshipped.' So I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I used to think, when Allah revealed: {He it is Who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it}, that this was completely fulfilled.' He said: 'There will occur of that whatever Allah wills; then Allah will send a pleasant wind that will take away everyone in whose heart is the weight of a mustard seed of faith, and there will remain those in whom there is no good, and they will revert to the religion of their forefathers.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—'Abd said: 'informed us', and Ibn Rafi' said: 'narrated to us'—'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until the buttocks of the women of Daws sway around Dhu al-Khalasah.' And it was an idol that Daws used to worship during the pre-Islamic period of ignorance at Tabalah.

'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn Aban, Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la, and Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Waki'i narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Aban's—they said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard Salim ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar saying: 'O people of Iraq! How often you ask about minor matters, while how readily you commit major sins! I heard my father, 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Indeed, tribulation comes from here"—and he pointed with his hand toward the East—"from where the two horns of Satan emerge." Yet you strike the necks of one another! Musa only killed the one he killed from the folk of Pharaoh by mistake, yet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to him: {And you killed a soul, but We delivered you from distress and tried you with trials}.' Ahmad ibn 'Umar said in his narration from Salim: he did not say 'I heard'.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Ishaq—meaning Ibn Sulayman—narrated to us: Hanzalah informed us, saying: I heard Salim saying: I heard Ibn 'Umar saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) pointing with his hand toward the East and saying: 'Behold, indeed the tribulation is right here! Behold, indeed the tribulation is right here!'—three times—'where the two horns of Satan emerge.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came out from the house of 'A'ishah and said: 'The head of disbelief is from right here, from where the horn of Satan emerges,' meaning the East.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said while facing the East: 'Behold, indeed the tribulation is right here! Behold, indeed the tribulation is right here! Behold, indeed the tribulation is right here, from where the horn of Satan emerges.'

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, all of them from Yahya al-Qattan; al-Qawariri said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar: Nafi' narrated to me, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stood near the door of Hafsah and gestured with his hand toward the East: 'The tribulation is right here, from where the horn of Satan emerges'—he said it twice or three times. And 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id said in his narration: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stood near the door of 'A'ishah.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us [H]; and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to me: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying while facing the East: 'Behold, indeed the tribulation is right here! Behold, indeed the tribulation is right here, from where the horn of Satan emerges.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Drought is not that you are given no rain; rather, drought is that you are given rain and given rain, yet the earth does not produce anything.'

'Amr an-Naqid narrated to me: Al-Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The dwellings will reach Ihab—or Yahab.' Zuhayr said: I said to Suhayl: 'How far is that from Medina?' He said: 'Such and such miles.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Ibn al-Musayyab informed me that Abu Hurayrah informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said [H]; and 'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me: my father narrated to us, from my grandfather: 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, that he said: Ibn al-Musayyab said: Abu Hurayrah informed me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until a fire emerges from the land of the Hijaz that will illuminate the necks of camels in Busra.'

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Abu an-Nu'man al-Hakam ibn 'Abdullah al-'Ijli narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Furat, who said: I heard Abu at-Tufayl narrating from Abu Sarihah, who said: We were talking when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came upon us... with the like of the hadith of Mu'adh and Ibn Ja'far. And Ibn al-Muthanna said: Abu an-Nu'man al-Hakam ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay', from Abu at-Tufayl, from Abu Sarihah, the like of it, and he said: 'and the tenth is the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam.' Shu'bah said: and 'Abd al-'Aziz did not raise it to the Prophet.
